Finding.Text: The added note says the kernel's XML reader supports elements, attributes, text and the XML declaration only. src/xml.ts also accepts comments (skipped before, inside and after the root element) and decodes the five predefined and numeric character references, as its header comment states. The exclusive "only" is therefore narrower than the reader; the part that matters, that a DOCTYPE, a CDATA section, a processing instruction or another encoding makes the reader throw and the change is reported malformed, was confirmed by probe (contract.xml with CDATA: "malformed: contract.xml: line 3: CDATA sections, processing instructions and declarations are not supported"; run-2.xml with a DOCTYPE or a processing instruction: "a root element was expected"; with encoding ISO-8859-1: "only UTF-8 documents are supported"). K2 asks each sentence to describe behaviour the kernel has; this one understates it. A wording fix, not a behaviour fix.

method.md closes with "Every later change to GRACE 5 is a change in its own repository whose Problem cites an explicit owner requirement, an invariant, or an observed failure, and which adds or amends one ledger entry", and the ledger header says "A change that adds or alters a mechanism adds or amends one entry here". This change amends two entries, L-09 and L-15, each in its cost column only, as K3 directs and the owner approved. I read "one" as at least one entry per mechanism whose limit is documented, two mechanisms being touched, and rule the verdict upheld; the literal count differs from the sentence, so the reading is on the record for the owner rather than inferred silently. No fix is required; if the owner reads "one" as exactly one, method.md or the contract is the place to say so.

Review.Adequacy: bun run check is tsc --noEmit over the kernel sources; it exits nonzero on any type error, so a pass separates a tree that still type-checks from one the change broke. For a change whose Constraint K1 forbids writing src/, this is a guard rather than a test of the delta; the delta itself is judged by the diff, which touches no .ts file. Rerun by the reviewer: exit 0.

bun test runs the conformance suite (60 tests across 4 files, 59 pass, 1 skip, the skip being the interrupted receipt that cannot be exercised on Windows per F10 of C-0001 review 6); any failing assertion exits nonzero. A pass separates an unchanged kernel from a regressed one, which is what A1 claims; it cannot show the absence of a source change, which the diff shows directly. The identical 59/1/0 counts on run-1 and run-2 are consistent with no behavioural change. Rerun by the reviewer.

bun run examples:verify reads every worked example with the kernel's own readContract and briefDefects, requires A to D to be clean and defective-brief to be reported with exactly the omitted protected path, and exits 1 otherwise (src/tools/examples-verify.ts). A pass separates examples the kernel still accepts from ones a document or schema change would have broken. Rerun by the reviewer: exit 0, same five lines as the logs.

bun run package:verify regenerates the three packages in memory from skills/ and from package.json's name, description, version and license, and the CLI reference from the help text, then compares byte for byte with packages/ and cli-reference.md, printing drift and exiting 1 on any difference or stray entry (src/tools/package.ts). This discriminates A3 directly: had plugin.json or openpackage.yml kept 0.0.0 while package.json says 0.1.0, or had they been hand-edited to anything but the generator's bytes, the run would have failed. That it also passed on run-1 (both sides 0.0.0) is correct, since the claim is agreement with the source, not a particular value. Rerun by the reviewer: ok for all four.

The command executes bun src/cli.ts --version and exits 0 only when the trimmed output equals exactly "grace5 0.1.0". kernelName() in src/records.ts reads the version from package.json, so the check binds the CLI's reported version to the intended value. Its failure mode was demonstrated: run-1 on the start revision recorded CK5 failed with exit 1 on version 0.0.0, and run-2 passed after the bump. Rerun by the reviewer: prints grace5 0.1.0, exit 0.
